answer: Reputation Decay Curve. Each new identity starts with a trust score that decays toward zero unless it completes verified interactions, and every agent action broadcasts a signed echo of its score history to peers. A single identity can spin up cheaply, but sustaining many in parallel forces each to keep earning independent reputation; the lagoon of low-score identities is throttled because downstream agents weight actions by score, so fake accounts produce no useful economic plume. An attacker pays the cumulative verification effort per identity plus the decay loss on idle ones.
